simple.meaning: הֲלַךְ (hălak) is a Hebrew word meaning “to walk.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הֲלַךְ (H1981) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:25, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֲלַךְ (H1981) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הֲלַךְ (H1981) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הֲלַךְ (hălak) / H1981 is traced through Daniel 3:25, Daniel 4:26, Daniel 4:34 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

timeline.evidenceText: He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”
Whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree; your kingdom shall be sure to you, after that you will have known that the heavens do rule.
At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever;
